pie: h₁súḱlewes nos gʷréh₂wō bʰindtó. puHróm moy toy gʷr̥h₂wéni mélh₂oh₂? h₁ím ml̥h₂dʰí gʷréh₂wō moy sénos. polh₁ús puHrós h₁ésti? h₁éy péh₂uros ḱósmi yéh₁ni ne h₂wérst. nu moy h₂léh₁wr̥ h₂r̥dʰí. túH n̥sméy lewbʰéh₂. mélit toy wésni h₁opéyōh₂. mélit ǵr̥h₂n̥tyéh₂bʰos gʷnéh₂bʰos sweh₂dú.
english: Of-Good-Fame, our quern split. May I grind my wheat on your quern? Grind it; my quern is old. Is there much wheat? There is little; it did not rain this year. Then take my flour. You are dear to us. I shall give you honey in the spring. Honey is sweet to old women.

pie: príHe toy wóǵʰos démi h₁ésti? dʰéyǵʰesi h₁épi stestóh₂e. kʷíd pr̥sḱési? dʰoHnéh₂ moy h₂éǵroy ḱéyor h₂wr̥syéh₁t-kʷe. h₁íh₂m̥ toy wóǵʰoh₁ dʰéh₁mn̥ h₁n̥dó wéǵʰōh₂. wóǵʰom h₁m̥dʰí dwóh₁-kʷe toy ugʷsénh₁e yugdʰí. kʷékʷlos sénos moḱs mē h₂éǵes. moḱs ne h₂éǵōh₂ dʰoHnéh₂m-kʷe toy h₁áyoh₂.
english: Friend, is your wagon at home? It is standing by the wall. Why do you ask? My grain is lying in the field, and it may rain. Let me carry it into the house with your wagon! Take the wagon, and yoke your two oxen. The wheel is old; do not drive quickly! I shall not drive quickly, and I shall give you grain.

pie: kʷíd moy pótey bʰoh₂gós h₃ésth₁? bʰréh₂tēr moy mḗms bʰágt. gʰóstey wékʷsperoy h₁ludʰés ḱwónes-kʷe mḗms h₁édn̥t. mḗms kʷéroy ne h₁ésti? h₁ésti mḗms. sddʰí úderom-kʷe toy pl̥nh₁dʰí. túH h₁wésus pótis. túH kénkonts gʰóstis.
english: Master, why is my share a bone? My brother got the meat as his share. Guest, you arrived in the evening, and the dogs were eating the meat. Is there no meat in the cauldron? There is meat. Sit down, and fill your belly! You are a good master. You are a hungry guest!

pie: tód ḱeḱluwṓs h₂ówis Héǵrom bʰugét.
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

pie: h₂éwh₂e nos ph₂tḗr ǵʰoysóm dʰénwr̥-kʷe likʷét. h₂réh₁dʰe nos. bʰréh₂tēr moy h₁eǵóh₂-kʷe dʰénwr̥ uḱwós. kʷóteros wos HéHḱyōs? h₁éy HéHḱyōs h₁eǵóh₂-kʷe méǵyōs. nu HeHḱús dʰénwr̥ sléh₂gʷtu méǵh₂s-kʷe ǵʰoysóm h₁éptu. h₂yúHn̥ḱoh₁ mē wikétom. h₂éwh₂e nos h₂réh₁dʰes méwdowos-kʷe.
english: Uncle, our father left a spear and a bow. Advise us! My brother and I want the bow. Which of you two is the swifter? He is swifter, and I am bigger. Then let the swift one take the bow, and let the big one grasp the spear. Do not fight, young men! You have advised us, uncle, and we two rejoice.

pie: eḱwos wewekur, "ḱludʰe, owei! ḱerd angʰetai widontbʰyos: ǵʰm̥on, potis, wl̥nam owiyōm kʷr̥neti soi gʷʰermom westrom; owibʰyos kʷe wl̥nā ne esti".
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

pie: h₁sń̥tyoḱlewes tísrn̥s wĺ̥kʷōm skéwHtins h₁idʰé wéǵʰom. wésmn̥ moy h₁íh₂mos siHwyé. kúdʰe wĺ̥kʷons moréyes? h₁íns snóygʷʰoy déh₂nu éti moréyom. nu túH wiHrós. h₁íd siHwyṓh₂ téntuns-kʷe moy ǵʰéresi. kúdʰe téntuns réh₁toh₂? swésorm̥ toy préḱsdʰi h₁íh₂ téksti. h₁íh₂ skéwHtim wélh₁eti.
english: Of-True-Fame, I carried three wolves' hides here. Sew me a garment from them! Where did you kill the wolves? I killed them beyond the river, in the snow. Then you are a hero! I shall sew it, and you shall fetch me threads. Where shall I find threads? Ask your sister; she weaves. She will want a hide.

pie: swésor méh₂tēr dwóh₁ pḱténh₁e tríh₂-kʷe usmń̥bʰis léykʷt. kʷóterom pḱténm̥ wéḱsi? túH h₂yuHn̥ḱéh₂ wl̥h₁dʰí. h₃sth₁és pḱténm̥ wélh₁m̥ h₂éyesos-kʷe pḱténm̥ h₁áyeth₂er. kʷíh₁ tríh₂ wésmn̥h₂ bʰéh₂gōwos? h₂énHōy nos h₁rudʰéh₁n̥t wésmn̥ déh₃owos. h₂énHos méwdeti h₁íd-kʷe dh₂pnóy wésetor.
english: Sister, mother left two combs and three garments. Which comb do you want? You are young; choose! I choose the comb of bone, and you shall receive the comb of bronze. And how shall we divide three garments? Let us give the red garment to our grandmother. Grandmother will rejoice, and she will wear it at the feast.

pie: ph₂ter moy wiḱpótis h₂éh₂usosyo péh₃tlom déh₃t. kʷíd h₁ésmey h₁áys? h₁ésmey kʷid ne h₁ā́m. nu h₁ésmey dóh₃r̥ dʰl̥gʰési. dóh₃r̥ déh₃rom wéḱti. kʷíd wiḱpóteyey h₁áyoh₂? h₁ésmey nos h₁wésistom moysóm h₁áydʰi h₁ím-kʷe dh₂pnóy gʷr̥nHdʰí. wiḱpótis nos démey priHós h₁syéh₁t. h₁éy h₁uséwōm déh₃tōr.
english: Father, the chief gave me a cup of gold. What did you give him? I gave him nothing. Then you owe him a gift. A gift wants a gift. What shall I give to the chief? Give him our best ram, and praise him at the feast. May the chief be dear to our house! He is a giver of good things.

pie: h₂éwh₂e moy séh₁mn̥ ǵʰiméni púHyet. kʷíd toy séh₁mn̥ púHyet? wódr̥ moy stégos h₁n̥dó gʷm̥yét h₁íd-kʷe ne widóm. séh₁mn̥ gʷʰédʰyoh₂ h₁íd-kʷe dʰǵʰémi séh₁yōh₂. kʷíd moy yéh₁ni déh₃esi? dwóyh₁ toy puHrósyo médesih₁ yéh₁ni déh₃oh₂. túH moy népōts. n̥ptés kʷid moy ne wéḱmi. h₂éwh₂e túH h₁wésus h₂nḗr péḱu toy h₂uksyéh₁t.
english: Uncle, my seed rotted in the winter. Why did your seed rot? Water came into my house, and I did not see it. I ask for seed, and I shall sow it in the earth. What will you give me at the harvest? At the harvest I shall give you two measures of wheat. You are my nephew. From my nephew I want nothing. You are a good man, uncle; may your herd grow!

pie: bʰréh₂ter nos ph₂tḗr mért. kʷíh₁ h₁ésyo gʷṓs bʰéh₂gōwos? déḱm̥ gʷṓs pénkʷe-kʷe h₁éḱwons léykʷt. gʷṓs dwís bʰéh₂gōwos pénkʷe-kʷe gʷṓs h₁émesi. kʷís h₁éḱwons sléh₂gʷeti? pr̥h₂wós ǵn̥h₁yóh₂e tríns-kʷe h₁éḱwons sléh₂gʷoh₂. nu moy HéHḱistom dh₃dʰí. túH h₂yuHn̥ḱós. HéHḱistom toy dédeh₃mi. túH h₁wésus bʰréh₂tēr.
english: Brother, our father has died. How shall we divide his cattle? He left ten cattle and five horses. Let us divide the cattle in two, and you shall take five cattle. And who will take the horses? I was born first, and I shall take three horses. Then give me the swiftest! You are young. I give you the swiftest. You are a good brother.

pie: wíḱpotey me ḱludʰí. h₂nér wr̥h₁dʰí. kʷíd h₂isḱési? swēḱurṓy moy h₁éḱwom péruti déh₃m̥ h₁ím-kʷe moy dṓm ne wédʰet. h₁éḱwom toy dʰl̥gʰéti? h₁ím moy dʰl̥gʰéti h₁óytom-kʷe h₃m̥néh₃t. nu dʰh₁tléh₂m gʷémtu ǵérh₂ontes-kʷe h₁ím ḱluwéntu. ǵérh₂ontes h₁sónt wr̥h₁ih₁ént.
english: Lord, hear me! Speak, man! What are you seeking? Last year I gave my horse to my brother-in-law, and he did not bring him to my house. Does he owe you the horse? He owes him to me, and he swore an oath. Then let him come to the assembly, and let the elders hear him. May the elders speak the truth!

pie: nókʷtm̥ pér bʰéwdʰōh₂? bʰéwdʰe dʰh₁méns-kʷe puHróm ph₂sdʰí. bʰóres kʷsépi gʷm̥sḱónti. bʰh₂dʰí moy h₁yód bʰṓr gʷémeti kʷíd dʰéh₁oh₂? HrudHdʰí wiHrṓs-kʷe bʰéwdʰonti. bʰr̥bʰós bʰebʰóyh₂h₂e. mē tréses tébʰye ḱóm légʰoh₂. nu ne bʰebʰóyh₂h₂e.
english: Shall I stay awake through the night? Stay awake, and guard the grain of the house. Thieves come at night. Speak to me: if a thief comes, what shall I do? Cry out, and the men will wake up. I am afraid of thieves. Do not tremble; I am lying beside you. Then I am not afraid.

pie: ǵérh₂ont toy h₂érh₃trom h₂éǵroy Hrumptó. kʷíh₁ Hrumptó? h₂éḱmonm̥ stunédt dóru-kʷe bʰindtó. polh₁éwes h₂éḱmones h₁énosmi h₂éǵroy h₁sénti. néwom moy h₂érh₃trom kʷéresi? pérkʷum kh₂éydōh₂ néwom-kʷe h₂érh₃trom wérǵoh₂. mē gʰrémes. ne gʰrémoh₂ h₂érh₃treh₂ Hrumptór.
english: Old man, your plough broke in the field. How did it break? It struck a stone, and the wood split. There are many stones in that field. Will you make me a new plough? I shall cut an oak, and I shall make a new plough. Do not be angry! I am not angry; ploughs break.

pie: h₂énHe stégesh₂ bʰindtó wódr̥-kʷe h₂élbʰit h₁n̥dó gʷm̥sḱéti. kúdʰe bʰindtó? dʰwóri upér bʰindtó. h₂élbʰit úd moḱs wéǵʰe h₁íd-kʷe ph₂wéni h₂sowséye. wéwke moy kʷís stégos stégēti? h₁íd lowbʰóh₁ gʰr̥h₁ménh₁-kʷe stégōh₂. dʰoHnéh₂ wédni púHyeti. lowbʰóm bʰeh₂ǵóybʰos skinédoh₂.
english: Grandmother, the roof split, and water is coming into the barley. Where did it split? It split above the door. Carry the barley out quickly, and dry it by the fire. Tell me: who will cover the roof? I shall cover it with bark and grass. Grain rots in water. I shall cut bark from the beeches.

pie: h₃réǵ gʷṓs póyḱoybʰos h₂éǵome. kʷóti moy déh₃esi? kʷóti póyḱons gʷʰéns? dwóh₁ tóh₁ gʷʰénm̥ dwóh₁-kʷe tóh₁ bʰugtā́m. nu kʷetwórn̥s gʷṓs bʰágesi. pr̥h₂wós gʷṓws pérkʷunōy h₁ésti. pérkʷunos n̥sméy wikét? póyḱōs h₁ésyo gʰrómōd trésont. nu spéh₁istom h₂r̥yéh₁t. h₂yúHn̥ḱe toy wíHre ḱléwos méǵh₂ h₁syéh₁t.
english: King, we drove the cattle away from the enemies. How many will you give to me? How many foes did you strike down? I struck down two, and two fled. Then you shall receive four cows as your share. The first cow is for Perkunos. Did Perkunos fight for us? The enemies trembled at his thunder. Then may he take the fattest! And may your fame be great, young warrior!

pie: gʷḗn dl̥h₁gʰóy h₂óǵmoy gʷm̥sḱóh₂. sḗh₂l moy lelóykʷe. kʷíd gʷʰédʰyesi? péh₂urom séh₂lm̥ gʷʰédʰyoh₂. h₂nér h₂Hséh₂i h₂énti sddʰí. séh₂lm̥ toy h₃éngʷn̥-kʷe dédeh₃mi. kúdʰe yéh₂si? swéḱurom moy pérwr̥ éti yéh₂mi. h₂éHsh₂ toy dʰégʷʰoyh₁t.
english: Woman, I am coming by a long way. My salt is gone. What are you asking for? I am asking for a little salt. Sit by the hearth, man. I give you salt and butter. Where are you going? I am going to my father-in-law beyond the mountain. May your hearth burn!

pie: kʷíh₁ méh₂ter h₁suh₁éḱwōy wéwkōh₂? h₁ésyo h₂érh₃trom wéḱmi. h₁ésmey ḱód wr̥h₁dʰí. h₁súh₁eḱwe moy toy h₂érh₃trom dh₃dʰí. h₂egʷnóm toy h₁opéyōh₂. h₁ésmey h₂egʷnóm h₁opéyōh₂? h₁opéye h₁éy-kʷe toy ḱéywos h₁éseti. h₁ésmey ḱód wérh₁oh₂.
english: Mother, how shall I speak to Of-Good-Horses? I want his plough. Say this to him: Of-Good-Horses, give me your plough! I shall give you a lamb. Shall I give him a lamb? Give it, and he will be dear to you. I shall say this to him.

pie: ḱwónn̥s nékʷti ḱléws? h₁íns ḱlḗm h₂élbʰit-kʷe moy h₂usési lelóykʷe. bʰṓr gʷémt. h₁ésyo lóysās déh₂newi widóm. kúdʰe gʷéh₂t? dóruh₂ próti gʷéh₂t. bʰórm̥ sékʷōmesdʰh₂ h₁ím-kʷe h₁épomes. h₁éyomes. ǵʰoysóm toy kapyé.
english: Did you hear the dogs in the night? I heard them, and at dawn my barley is gone. A thief came! I saw his tracks at the river. Where did he go? He went toward the trees. Let us follow the thief, and let us seize him. Let us go! Grasp your spear!

pie: kʷíd ph₂ter bʰoh₂gós? h₁yód bʰréh₂teres gʷṓs bʰéh₂gonti bʰoh₂góns sl̥h₂gʷént. bʰoh₂góm bʰágoh₂? súHnew h₁ím bʰágesi swésores-kʷe toy h₁wédm̥nih₁ bʰágonti. kʷíd h₁wédmn̥? h₁wédmn̥ péḱu h₁yód h₁ésyeh₂s pótim dʰugh₂tréh₁ ḱóm h₁éyti. nu dʰugh₂tḗr h₁syéh₁m̥. smḗysi túH-kʷe moy suHnús.
english: Father, what is a share? When brothers divide the cattle, they take shares. Shall I receive a share? You shall receive one, son, What is a dowry? A dowry is the livestock which goes with a daughter to her husband. Then may I be a daughter! You laugh, and you are my son.

pie: h₂éwh₂e moy wéwke. kʷíd gʰostíbʰos déh₃ōr dedh₃més? h₁yós gʰostéyey h₁opéyeti só priHóm winédti. linékʷti h₂ew-kʷe ne gʷm̥yéti. h₁yód dweh₂róy stóygʰoy stéygʰēsi gʰóstis h₂én h₁ésesi. nu kʷis toy médʰu légʰos-kʷe déh₃eti. nu dóh₃r̥ déh₃torm̥ h₂ew gʷm̥yéti. nu népot h₁íd wóydth₂e.
english: Grandfather, tell me! Why do we give gifts to guests? He who gives to a guest, he finds a friend. But he goes away, and he does not come again. When you walk on a far road, you will be a guest there. Then someone will give you mead and a bed. Then the gift comes to the giver again. Now you know it, grandson.

pie: méh₂ter mē gʰrémes. ḱéstrom toy lelóykʷe. kúdʰe h₁és? déh₂newi snā́m ḱéstrom-kʷe wédni néḱt. h₁íd h₂isḱés? h₁íd h₂isḱóm h₁íd-kʷe ne winédm̥. nu moy ḱéstrom dʰl̥gʰési. dʰh₂bʰróm gʷh₂dʰí h₁ésmey-kʷe wr̥ǵdʰí. moḱs gʷéh₂oh₂.
english: Mother, do not be angry! Your knife is gone. Where were you? I was swimming in the river, and the knife vanished in the water. Did you search for it? I searched for it, but I did not find it. Then you owe me a knife. Go to the smith, and work for him! I shall go early.

pie: déywoǵenh₁es nésm̥. méh₂tēr nos wékʷsperoysu HréwdHt. skʷdʰí moy gʷíh₃weti? gʷíh₃weti h₂Hséh₂i-kʷe h₂énti sedéh₁yeti. kúdʰe moy péḱu h₁ésti? ph₂tḗr nos moy h₁íd léykʷt. tébʰye h₁íd péh₂sm̥ h₂wékst-kʷe. túH moy ḱéywōm. moysóm gʷʰénowos ph₂wéni-kʷe h₁édowos.
english: Of-Divine-Race, I have come home unharmed. Our mother cried in the evenings. Tell me: is she alive? She lives, and she sits by the hearth. Where is my herd? Our father left it to me. I guarded it for you, and it grew. You are dear to me. Let us kill a ram, and let us eat by the fire!

pie: h₁súmenes toy kʷéros h₁idʰé h₁ésti. kʷíd h₁éy gʷr̥h₂ús? suHés sélpos h₁ésmi h₁ésti. dh₂pnṓy súHm̥ gʷʰn̥mé. ne moy kʷid dʰl̥gʰési kʷíd moy sélpos h₁opéyesi? kʷérom moy toy déh₃s sélpos-kʷe toy dédeh₃mi. nu wiḱdʰí n̥sméy-kʷe ḱóm h₁ddʰí. téḱnōys moy ḱóm gʷémoh₂. h₁íh₂ wédʰe pótim moy moysóm pékʷeti.
english: Kindly, your cauldron is here. Why is it heavy? There is pig's fat in it. We killed a pig for the feast. You owe me nothing; why do you give me fat? You gave me your cauldron, and I give you fat. Then come in, and eat with us! I shall come with my children. Bring them; my husband is cooking a ram.

pie: pótni toy médʰu sweh₂dú h₁ést mā́dsos-kʷe toy swéh₂dyōs h₁ést. kʷíd toy dʰl̥gʰóh₂? kéh₂nmn̥ moy séngʷʰe. polh₁úm mā́dsom h₂éḱh₃s kʷetwṓr-kʷe péh₃tleh₂ péh₃s. h₁yód gʷéHyoh₂ gʷówes tr̥ménti. nu gʷowsth₂óy h₁épi gʷéHye. ḱléwesos toy kéh₂nmn̥ séngʷʰōh₂. h₁íd h₂Hséh₂i h₂énti séngʷʰe sméyoh₂-kʷe. pótni mē smḗys.
english: Mistress, your mead was sweet, and your mush was sweeter. What do I owe you? Sing me a song! You ate much mush, and you drank four cups. When I sing, the cows tremble. Then sing at the cow-stall! I shall sing a song of your fame. Sing it by the hearth, and I shall laugh. Do not laugh, mistress!

pie: péḱu toy moy gʰréh₁mn̥ gʷr̥h₃ét gʰórdʰom-kʷe moy Hrunépt. h₁íd swṓys h₃kʷbʰís widés? h₁íd swṓys h₃kʷbʰís widóm. h₂nŕ̥menes mē gʰrémes. néwom toy gʰórdʰom démōh₂ káprom-kʷe toy déh₃oh₂. káprom h₂egʷnóm-kʷe wéḱmi. h₂nŕ̥menes túH wĺ̥kʷos. káprom h₁m̥dʰí priHóh₁-kʷe h₁ésowos. kápros néwos-kʷe gʰórdʰos.
english: Your cattle ate my grass, and they broke my fence! Did you see it with your own eyes? I saw it with my own eyes. Do not be angry, Man-Minded. I shall build you a new fence, and I shall give you a goat. I want a goat and a lamb! You are a wolf, Man-Minded! Take the goat, and let us be friends. A goat and a new fence!

pie: owis, yesmin wl̥nā ne ēst, dedorḱe eḱwons wogʰom gʷr̥um wegʰontn̥s, bʰorom meǵHm, monum ōḱu bʰerontn̥s.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: gʷḗn moy wésmn̥ tksdʰí. h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m bʰéres? tisróHom h₂éwyōm h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m bʰérom. kʷésmey wésmn̥ h₁ésti? h₁íd moy bʰréh₂trey h₁ésti dl̥h₁gʰóy-kʷe stóygʰoy h₁éyti. nu h₁íd téksoh₂ ǵʰiméni-kʷe gʷʰréh₁yēti. kʷíd toy dédeh₃oh₂? h₂mélǵos moy mélit-kʷe bʰére.
english: Woman, weave me a garment! Did you bring wool? I brought the wool of three sheep. For whom is the garment? It is for my brother, and he is going on a long road. Then I shall weave it, and he will be warm in the winter. What shall I give you? Bring me milk and honey!
